note: Where a person can actually go and acquire a credential, keyed by TRUST ROOT rather than by adapter — because acquiring a second credential in a root you already hold raises nothing. This is the routing half of the aggregator: the registry says what evidence is worth, this says where to get the evidence you are missing. Deliberately NOT on-chain: these are UX pointers that rot, not weights that need an audit trail. Every URL was fetched and returned 200 on 2026-07-25 except Coinbase, which 403s non-browser clients (same as base.org) and was confirmed by inspection.
privacyNote: Each entry states what the enrolment costs you, not only what it gains. A score is not worth a permanent public biometric if you did not want one.

iris-registry:world-orb.name: World ID — Orb verification
iris-registry:world-orb.effort: In person at an Orb, ~5 minutes
iris-registry:world-orb.youGive: An iris scan. The iris code is not stored, but a stable global identifier for you is published on a public chain.
iris-registry:world-orb.note: The cheapest single credential to rent at scale, which is why we price it at $0.50 rather than the cost of the hardware.

state-document:icao-9303.name: ZKPassport
state-document:icao-9303.effort: Phone with NFC, tap your passport, ~2 minutes
state-document:icao-9303.youGive: Nothing linkable. Nullifiers are scoped per service, so this credential cannot be correlated across apps — including by us.
state-document:icao-9303.note: Strongest privacy in the roster. The trade-off is that we cannot read it unsolicited; a consumer who verifies the proof has to hand it to us.

state-document:icao-9303.name: Self
state-document:icao-9303.effort: Phone with NFC, tap your passport
state-document:icao-9303.youGive: A globally scoped nullifier, so this one IS correlatable across apps.
state-document:icao-9303.note: Same passport chip as ZKPassport, therefore the same trust root. Holding both adds nothing to your independence.

social-vouching:poh.name: Proof of Humanity
social-vouching:poh.effort: Video submission plus a voucher who already registered, then a challenge period
social-vouching:poh.price: A refundable deposit, plus gas on Gnosis
social-vouching:poh.youGive: A public video of your face and voice, permanently, on IPFS. This is the least private option here by a wide margin.
social-vouching:poh.note: Weighted on a survival ramp, so it is worth little at first and more as it survives challenge windows. Do not expect an immediate score.

social-trust:circles.name: Circles
social-trust:circles.effort: Needs an invitation from someone already in the graph
social-trust:circles.price: Free to you — the inviter spends four days of their own issuance
social-trust:circles.youGive: A public position in a social trust graph. No document, no biometric, no liveness check anywhere in the protocol.
social-trust:circles.note: Registration alone is near-worthless as evidence; what carries signal is who trusts you and how well-connected they are.

kyc-vendor:persona.name: Coinbase Onchain Verification
kyc-vendor:persona.effort: A Coinbase account that has completed identity verification
kyc-vendor:persona.youGive: A full KYC file to Coinbase and its vendor. The attestation itself is public on Base.
kyc-vendor:persona.note: Persona-rooted, so it shares a root with every other Persona-backed credential. Over half of these have been revoked, so we check revocation explicitly.

behavioral:wallet-history.name: Human Passport
behavioral:wallet-history.youGive: Links between your wallets and social accounts — which is a correlation you may not want to publish.
behavioral:wallet-history.note: Mostly a republisher of other people's credentials. We root it in wallet history so its own stamps do not get counted twice against their real issuers.

social-account:farcaster.name: Farcaster account
social-account:farcaster.price: About $0.44 to register plus ~$0.20/yr on chain
social-account:farcaster.note: Weak as personhood evidence and priced accordingly. Useful mainly as an independent root when you have few others.

kyc-vendor:facetec.name: Holonym / Human Network
kyc-vendor:facetec.effort: Government ID or a face scan, minutes
kyc-vendor:facetec.youGive: Either a government document or biometrics, to a vendor.
kyc-vendor:facetec.note: FaceTec's 1:N deduplication is per-integrator and never global, so this yields liveness rather than genuine uniqueness.

ceremony:encointer.name: Encointer
ceremony:encointer.effort: Attend an in-person key-signing meetup at a fixed time and place
ceremony:encointer.youGive: Your physical presence at a specific place and time, to strangers.
ceremony:encointer.note: The only root here with the property Ohlhaver argues actually matters: one person cannot physically show up as two.

biometric-registry:humanode.name: Humanode
biometric-registry:humanode.youGive: Face biometrics to a private registry.
biometric-registry:humanode.note: Uniqueness is enforced inside Humanode's own set only.

social-account:lens.name: Lens account
social-account:lens.youGive: A public social account. Ownership transfers need no recipient consent, so an account can also be planted on an address that never asked for it.
social-account:lens.note: Priced at 1¢ — below the independence floor by design. It never moves a score; what it adds is texture: a username, an acquisition date, and someday graph position.

kyc-vendor:sumsub.name: Galxe Passport
kyc-vendor:sumsub.effort: Government ID plus a liveness check, minutes
kyc-vendor:sumsub.youGive: A full KYC file to Sumsub, Galxe's vendor. The soulbound token itself is public on BNB Chain.
kyc-vendor:sumsub.note: Shares its trust root with Linea PoH — holding both counts once.

kyc-vendor:sumsub.name: Linea Proof of Humanity
kyc-vendor:sumsub.effort: Government ID plus a liveness check via a partner, minutes
kyc-vendor:sumsub.youGive: A KYC file to Sumsub via one of Linea's attestation partners.
kyc-vendor:sumsub.note: Shares its trust root with Galxe Passport — holding both counts once.

kyc-vendor:unattributed.name: Holonym / Human Network — government ID
kyc-vendor:unattributed.youGive: A government document to a vendor whose downstream KYC processor is not publicly attributed — which is why this root is priced separately from the named vendors.
kyc-vendor:unattributed.note: Distinct root from Holonym's biometric path (FaceTec); holding both is two roots.
